Layers 1 to 5, in order

The decision sheet

Twenty-five things to confirm and fifteen things that end the plan, arranged so that failure stays cheap.

Twenty-five checks, in the order they can kill the project. Work top to bottom: a failed check in Layer 1 is not fixed by a better structure in Layer 3. The fifteen stop conditions at the end are not risks to manage; they are reasons to stop and change the plan.

This is a reading aid, not a filing. Nothing here is saved to a server — the boxes use your browser's own storage and can be cleared at any time.

!

Stop conditions

Any one of these ends the plan, whatever the other layers say

Print this page and take it to your lawyer. A ticked box is your own answer, not evidence — the sheet exists to show you which answers you have not actually checked.

What this sheet is not. It is not a legal opinion, a valuation, or a prediction. It does not tell you whether the business will work. It is a way of finding out, in ten minutes and for nothing, whether a plan you are considering fails on the first two layers — which is where most plans by foreign founders actually fail.

If you want the reasoning behind any line, follow it back to the framework. If you want the vocabulary you will hear at the counter, the glossary has the terms that come up most often, with the characters you will see on paper.
